geometry_edits.rationale: Increase courtyard depth to strengthen the public open-space figure without changing the dominant compact mass.
Keep the courtyard opening aligned to the access side to reinforce the entry threshold.

graph_edits.rationale: Keep the dominant courtyard gesture but make the public void more assertive and legible at the street edge.
Slightly enlarge the carve so the void reads as a usable public court rather than a thin residual.
Align the open side to the verified access side so the ground response is semantically aligned with arrival.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent early-stage neighborhood-living mass: a compact low bar with a central courtyard/void and a clear open top view. It responds plausibly to the parcel and avoids obvious view-to-view collisions, so it passes the hard visual containment/coherence gate. The main weakness is that the silhouette is still somewhat boxy and the street-edge response is not yet fully articulated as a strong public threshold; the void exists, but it could be more legible as a ground-level entry/court condition aligned to access. Programmatically it is close enough for neighborhood living because it offers one dominant occupied volume, an articulated void, and a calm upper massing, but it is not yet exemplary in section or edge hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more sculptural and pavilion-like than this compact neighborhood building; do not copy the curved roof language literally.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part massing with a carved central void and a bridge-like upper connector creates a readable public threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Scale is much larger and more complex; the candidate should stay compact and avoid campus fragmentation.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, campus-like arrangement around a central court supports collective public space while preserving clear hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate already has a courtyard-like subtraction; avoid over-boxifying the form further.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A strong rectangular mass becomes legible through a large cutout/void and shallow setback at ground level.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference leans more openly glazed and site-responsive; the candidate needs a clearer access-edge response.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: An elongated low-rise mass can host a central atrium/void while keeping a calm horizontal profile.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is more dispersed and connected than the candidate; retain compactness and strengthen the street threshold instead of adding wings.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Spread-out low massing with bridging and terraced/courtyard space can support neighborhood-scale public life.

warnings: The form is strongest in plan/top view; the section and access-edge expression are less resolved.
The central void is present but could read as more publicly usable and less like a simple subtraction.
The mass still trends toward a generic extruded ring; a cleaner anchor or a more explicit carved entry seam would improve program clarity.
